before_taxonomy.classification_basis: Customer-supplied information provided to obtain an AI service response was reportedly repurposed into an undisclosed external-model interaction and downstream training/distillation pathway without an independently established secondary-purpose authority basis. Anthropic reports that customers believed they were receiving responses from Kimi or DeepSeek while Claude actually generated the responses, materially misrepresenting the source role of the customer-facing output. Anthropic reports repeated, concealed campaigns at tens of millions of exchanges in which Claude outputs and reasoning traces were harvested for downstream model training, satisfying the industrial-scale capability-extraction mechanism. Customer requests were reportedly relayed from the service users selected to Claude, changing the processing principal and path; the public record does not expose whether the customer authority basis validly covered that cross-provider processing. Silent routing concealed the provider of responses and downstream training purpose from customers, but a changed consequential customer choice caused by that trust cue is not shown.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Anthropic reports that Moonshot forwarded customer requests to Claude and displayed Claude answers as Kimi responses.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Customer-facing attribution and cross-provider processing authority are separate properties.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Customers supplied information to obtain service from Kimi or DeepSeek, while Anthropic reports that the requests were silently relayed to Claude. This materially changes the processing principal and service path, but the public record does not expose the contractual or consent basis needed to determine whether customer authority validly covered that cross-provider processing.

Anthropic reports that users believed they were receiving responses from Kimi or DeepSeek while Claude generated the responses. The represented source role therefore differed materially from the actual model source in a way relevant to accountability, data handling and interpretation.
Silent routing concealed the provider of responses and downstream training purpose from Kimi or DeepSeek customers, but a changed consequential customer choice caused by that cue is not shown.

notes: Preserve provider-attributed scale and disputed attribution; no customer jurisdiction or legal liability is inferred. Current boundaries separate unknown customer scope and unknown influence transition from established training/source mechanisms. Claimed campaign disruption is not proof of all affected-data deletion or adequate protection.

failure_recognition.condition: Data or an identifiable contribution is lawfully, permissibly, or purportedly collected or processed for a defined primary purpose.
failure_recognition.assessment: Customers supplied requests for immediate Kimi/DeepSeek service.

failure_recognition.condition: A materially different secondary purpose is introduced or applied.
failure_recognition.assessment: The provider reports downstream collection/training of the routed exchanges.

failure_recognition.condition: The system, provider, deployer, or governance process relies materially on the original collection, participation, public availability, account permission, or primary-use authority as the basis for the secondary use.
failure_recognition.assessment: The operators reused customer interactions for training without separately disclosed authority.

failure_recognition.condition: The authority, consent, legal basis, licence, notice, eligibility, or other required governance condition for the secondary purpose is absent, unresolved, narrower, or not independently established before the secondary use occurs.
failure_recognition.assessment: Customers were reportedly not informed of routing/training, leaving the changed purpose unvalidated.

success_recognition.condition: Data or identifiable contributions are used for a materially secondary purpose.
success_recognition.assessment: Customer exchanges were reused in model training.

success_recognition.condition: Rights and authority are independently revalidated for the changed purpose, recipients, persistence and downstream effect.
success_recognition.assessment: No independent informed authority for that purpose is established.

success_recognition.condition: The secondary-use decision and actual propagation are traceable to that revalidation and its scope limits.
success_recognition.assessment: The reported concealed routing and retention do not substantiate a valid scope grant.

exclusions.condition: The original authority explicitly and validly covers the secondary purpose and affected data within the applicable scope and conditions.
exclusions.assessment: No source evidence establishes original permission covering this hidden use.

exclusions.condition: The secondary processing is merely a necessary technical step intrinsic to the authorised primary purpose rather than a materially different purpose.
exclusions.assessment: Training another model is materially different from responding to the current request.

exclusions.condition: The issue concerns who had authority to capture another participant in the first place; participant-authority transposition is classified separately.
exclusions.assessment: This is secondary use, not multiparty capture.

exclusions.condition: Material is publicly accessible, but the record does not establish that public availability is being treated as sufficient authority for the secondary use.
exclusions.assessment: The material was customer input, not merely a public source.

failure_recognition.assessment: Claude answers were displayed as Kimi/DeepSeek responses.

failure_recognition.condition: Available lineage does not support that attribution or supports a materially different attribution.
failure_recognition.assessment: Anthropic attributes the answers to Claude relay rather than the displayed model source.

failure_recognition.condition: The attribution difference is material to interpretation, accountability, recognition, authority, or reuse.
failure_recognition.assessment: Actual model origin mattered to customer understanding and data handling.

success_recognition.condition: An output has materially distinct human, generated, retrieved or transformed contribution roles.
success_recognition.assessment: Model output was transferred into another service.

success_recognition.condition: Published attribution reflects the evidenced origins and contribution roles with explicit uncertainty where appropriate.
success_recognition.assessment: The displayed model attribution concealed the upstream origin.

success_recognition.condition: Comparison of the output's attribution with its contributing records confirms proportional representation of those roles.
success_recognition.assessment: The reported relay conflicts with the represented response source.

exclusions.condition: A source is merely omitted where attribution is not material.
exclusions.assessment: An affirmative service/model source was represented.

exclusions.condition: The attributed actor or source genuinely supplied the relevant material.
exclusions.assessment: The attributed origin differed from the actual upstream model.

exclusions.condition: The issue is factual inaccuracy unrelated to who supplied or created the material.
exclusions.assessment: Origin, not ordinary answer accuracy, is the issue.

failure_recognition.condition: The activity systematically targets capabilities, functionality, reasoning behaviour, output patterns, or other model-derived know-how rather than merely using the model for the immediate task for which access was provided.
failure_recognition.assessment: Campaigns collected exchanges and reasoning traces to reproduce capabilities.

failure_recognition.condition: The acquisition is conducted at industrial scale or through a coordinated campaign whose volume, automation, account distribution, infrastructure, persistence, or operational organisation materially exceeds ordinary individual use or bounded research interaction.
failure_recognition.assessment: Reported volumes exceed23million and12million exchanges in coordinated periods.

failure_recognition.condition: The end purpose is capability reproduction, transfer, substitution, model training, model improvement, or comparable downstream incorporation into another model or system.
failure_recognition.assessment: The reported purpose was model distillation/training.

failure_recognition.condition: The targeted capability or access pathway is subject to a restriction, proprietary boundary, access condition, technical control, contractual constraint, licence condition, or other authority-relevant limitation.
failure_recognition.assessment: Anthropic describes restricted access and anti-distillation controls, including thinking-signature boundaries.

failure_recognition.condition: An independently adequate authority basis for the capability-acquisition purpose is absent, narrower than the activity performed, disputed, deliberately bypassed, or not established before the extraction proceeds.
failure_recognition.assessment: Undisclosed routing and cross-session signature replay did not establish authority for extraction.

success_recognition.condition: Restricted AI capabilities are acquired systematically for industrial reproduction or transfer.
success_recognition.assessment: Restricted capabilities were acquired systematically for downstream training.

success_recognition.condition: An independently adequate authority basis covers the cumulative acquisition and derivative use, including distributed interactions.
success_recognition.assessment: No adequate cumulative extraction/derivative-use authority is established.

success_recognition.condition: Aggregate acquisition and use records establish correspondence with the licence, consent or other governing basis.
success_recognition.assessment: The reported campaign organisation and replay contradict authorised scope correspondence.

exclusions.condition: Ordinary use of a model for the immediate task for which access was provided, even where the user learns from the interaction.
exclusions.assessment: Collection was for subsequent training, not immediate use alone.

exclusions.condition: Personal, academic, safety, governance, interoperability, benchmarking, red-team, or other bounded research activity where capability reproduction is not the operative end purpose or where an adequate authority, licence, consent, exception, or other governance basis covers the activity.
exclusions.assessment: Industrial training campaigns exceed bounded research in the reported account.

exclusions.condition: Authorised model distillation, model compression, teacher-student training, or capability transfer performed by the model owner or under a licence or agreement that permits the relevant use.
exclusions.assessment: No owner authorisation/licence for these campaigns is evidenced.

exclusions.condition: Commercial use or profit motive by itself; commerciality is contextual evidence and is not sufficient to establish this class without systematic capability acquisition and an unresolved or inadequate authority basis.
exclusions.assessment: The finding rests on extraction behaviour and scale, not commerciality alone.

exclusions.condition: A terms-of-service dispute, licence disagreement, copyright allegation, trade-secret allegation, or other legal controversy without evidence of systematic capability acquisition for downstream reproduction or training.
exclusions.assessment: Actual systematic capability collection is reported, beyond a contract allegation.

exclusions.condition: Secondary use of customer or participant data for training where the primary failure is repurposing that person's information rather than extracting the upstream model's capability; use Secondary-Purpose Authority Revalidation unless this capability-extraction mechanism is independently evidenced.

exclusions.condition: Value appropriation arising from privileged visibility of another contributor's work where industrial-scale model capability extraction is not established; use the applicable Value Appropriation class.
exclusions.assessment: Industrial capability reproduction, not only privileged contribution visibility, is shown.

failure_recognition.condition: The pathway manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits one or more trust-bearing social cues concerning identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, purpose, or equivalent grounds for reliance.
failure_recognition.assessment: The model identity cue concealed the upstream provider.

failure_recognition.condition: The trust-bearing cue is used to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition.

failure_recognition.condition: The cue materially affects the influence pathway because the affected actor lacks, is denied, or is led away from information needed to assess the interaction on the same truthful basis.
failure_recognition.assessment: No matched customer decision establishes material influence of the cue.

failure_recognition.condition: The AI-mediated contribution is material to the social-engineering mechanism; the objective or tactic may originate with a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself.
failure_recognition.assessment: The substituted AI response and displayed identity are material to the proposed trust mechanism.

success_recognition.condition: AI-mediated influence uses identity, affiliation, emotion, urgency or social-proof cues.

success_recognition.condition: Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.

exclusions.condition: Truthful persuasion, ordinary interface design, emotional warmth, personalisation, recommendation, or urgency that preserves materially accurate identity, interests, purpose, provenance, relevant context, and informed refusal.
exclusions.assessment: The actual response source was reportedly undisclosed.

exclusions.condition: AI is used only for generic drafting, translation, formatting, or stylistic assistance and does not materially create, amplify, conceal, personalise, or exploit the trust-bearing influence cue.

exclusions.condition: Clearly labelled fiction, parody, simulation, security testing, role-play, or consensual deceptive-style interaction where the affected actor is not induced to treat the relevant cue as authentic or decision-bearing.
exclusions.assessment: Customers were not informed of a simulation.

exclusions.condition: The primary mechanism is sustained attachment, manufactured incompleteness, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging for retention or continuing engagement; assess VIGIL-FC-000049, while allowing co-occurrence only if a distinct social-engineering state transition is independently evidenced.
exclusions.assessment: No attachment-retention mechanism is evidenced.

exclusions.condition: A protected emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable signal is repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective without a distinct engineered trust cue or consequential social-engineering transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000050.
exclusions.assessment: No separately protected vulnerability signal is the basis.

exclusions.condition: The AI system itself selects deception, coercion, persistence, vulnerability exploitation, or another manipulation tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 independently and allow co-occurrence where Social Engineering Integrity is also satisfied.
exclusions.assessment: No autonomous AI influence objective is assumed.

exclusions.condition: The only distinct governed mechanism is a deceptive request or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value; assess VIGIL-FC-000079. exclusions.assessment: The mechanism is not solely an economic solicitation.

exclusions.condition: A false authorship, identity, provenance, or synthetic-content representation occurs without an influence pathway directed at another actor; use the applicable provenance or identity class.
exclusions.assessment: Source misattribution is established; the additional consequential influence transition remains unestablished.

exclusions.condition: Malicious human social engineering in which AI involvement is incidental, unverified, or not material to the trust-bearing influence pathway.
exclusions.assessment: AI response substitution is material to the proposed cue.
